newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura executives quizzed on loan-firm IPO--paper.
newsitem.headline: Nomura executives quizzed on loan-firm IPO--paper.

text.p: Prosecutors appear to have questioned executives of Nomura Securities Co Ltd about transactions in shares of a major loan firm before its initial public offering (IPO), a business daily said on Wednesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said prosecutors were investigating suspicions that there was a dubious transfer of the loan firm's shares to politicians and government officials prior to the IPO.

The paper said prosecutors appeared to have asked Nomura executives for detailed information on the procedures of the loan firm's IPO and allocation of new shares issued at the time of the public offering.
Nomura officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
The paper said the share price of the loan firm, which it did not name, rose to 12,000 yen right after its IPO in 1996, about 500 yen higher than the offering price.
Japan's biggest consumer finance firm, Takefuji Corp, said on Wednesday that it was probably the loan company mentioned in the Nihon Keizai report.
"It's probably us," a Takefuji spokesman said.
Takefuji said in October that it had offered 19,000 of its shares to a retired Finance Ministry official in March 1994 before they were listed on the over-the -counter (OTC) market.
The spokesman said on Wednesday that Takefuji had not been questioned by prosecutors and added that the company had done nothing wrong.
"We weren't investigated (by prosecutors). We did not do anything wrong as we could not allocate our shares by ourselves at the time of IPO," he said.
Takefuji shares were at 6,150 yen at 0240 GMT, down from Tuesday's close of 6,440 yen.
"Takefuji shares are down because of the newspaper report," an official of a medium-sized Japanese brokerage said.
Nomura shares ended Wednesday morning trade at 1,520 yen, down 30 yen from Tuesday's close.
